note: Engine v2 rerun list: real-16 + known-10 + known-5, pinned to the same commits as the v1 audits so v1 vs v2 compare like for like

suspectedDrift.what: README clone-then-cd instructions reference a directory name that doesn't exist
suspectedDrift.evidence: README.md 'Install, Configure & Run': `git clone https://github.com/GeekyAnts/express-typescript.git;` immediately followed by `cd nodets;` — the cloned folder is named `express-typescript`, not `nodets`, so the very next command fails.

suspectedDrift.what: Stated Node floor is far below what the toolchain actually needs, with nothing to verify either number
suspectedDrift.evidence: README.md 'Global Requisites' says `node (>= 10.5.0)`; package.json devDependencies pin `typescript: 5.0.3` and `@types/node: ^12.12.17`; there is no CI workflow in .github/workflows at all, so neither claim is ever exercised.

suspectedDrift.what: Non-Docker instructions omit the Redis dependency that the app actually needs
suspectedDrift.evidence: README.md 'Without Docker' block's only prerequisite note is 'It is assumed here that you have MongoDB running'; package.json depends on `kue` (a Redis-backed queue) and the committed `.env` ships REDIS_QUEUE_* variables, but Redis is only mentioned in the separate 'Global Requisites' bullet list, not in the run steps themselves.

repos.why: Guaranteed literal command failure (cd into a nonexistent directory) makes this the fastest, cleanest 'the README is just wrong' demo, plus two more independent real gaps behind it.

suspectedDrift.what: The running server never actually opens a MongoDB connection
suspectedDrift.evidence: app.js (66 lines total) has no `mongoose.connect()` call anywhere; the only `mongoose.connect(mongoDB)` in the whole repo is in populatedb.js:28, a standalone script that takes the URI as a CLI argument and is never invoked from app.js/bin/www. models/author.js, book.js, bookinstance.js, genre.js all `require('mongoose')` and define schemas that will hang or error on first query since nothing initializes the connection.

suspectedDrift.what: README's Quick Start never asks for a Mongo URI at all
suspectedDrift.evidence: README.md lines 17-35 list only `npm install` then `npm run devstart` / `npm start`; no .env step, no connection-string prompt. The only DB guidance is the note at README.md:39-40 that 'the library uses a default MongoDB database hosted on MongoDB Atlas' — no URI given, no .env.example shipped in the repo.

repos.why: Actively-maintained MDN teaching repo (pushed days ago) whose own catalog pages will 500 on first visit because nothing in app.js ever connects to Mongo — a strong 'well-maintained but drifted' story.

repos.readmeSetupSection: Getting Started (Run Locally / Run with Docker)

suspectedDrift.what: docker-compose points the app at the wrong internal MySQL port
suspectedDrift.evidence: docker-compose.yml: the `mysql` service maps `'3307:3306'` (host:container) but `auth-service`'s DATABASE_URL is hardcoded to `mysql://root:${MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD}@mysql:3307/${MYSQL_DATABASE}`. Container-to-container traffic on the compose network must hit the container's actual listening port (3306); 3307 is only the host-side remap, so `docker-compose up` boots but the app can never reach the DB.

suspectedDrift.what: README never mentions applying Prisma migrations
suspectedDrift.evidence: README.md 'Run Locally' / 'Run with Docker' sections go straight from 'define the .env variables' to `yarn dev` / `docker-compose up`. package.json has no `prisma migrate` or `postinstall` script, and prisma/schema.prisma defines real models, but no step anywhere creates the tables before the app starts.

repos.why: Two independent, concrete, container-specific bugs (wrong port + missing migration step) that only surface once someone actually tries the Docker path — exactly FirstRun's use case.

suspectedDrift.what: The repo's own 'Quick Start' doesn't set up this repo at all — it clones a different repo
suspectedDrift.evidence: README.md lines 82-90, 'Quick Start' step 1: `git clone https://github.com/JKHeadley/rest-hapi-demo.git` then `cd rest-hapi-demo`, not this repository (rest-hapi). rest-hapi-demo was itself last pushed 2022-12-02, over two years before this README's last update, and is a separate scaffolded project, not this library's source.

repos.why: A maximally clean example of README drift: following the literal 'Quick Start' takes a newcomer out of the audited repo entirely, into a second, differently-maintained repo.

suspectedDrift.what: Celery's broker defaults to RabbitMQ, which nothing in the setup path provisions or mentions
suspectedDrift.evidence: core/config.py:17 default `CELERY_BROKER_URL: str = "amqp://user:bitnami@localhost:5672/"` (RabbitMQ/AMQP); docker/docker-compose.yml only defines `mysql` and `redis` services; README.md 'Run' section's only infra step is `docker-compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml up` — RabbitMQ is never mentioned anywhere in the README.

repos.why: Real missing-service gap (code wants RabbitMQ, compose/README only give Redis+MySQL) on an actively maintained, very popular FastAPI boilerplate.

suspectedDrift.what: README skips the Alembic migration step entirely
suspectedDrift.evidence: README.md 'Local Development' order is `just up` (start Postgres) -> `cp .env.example .env` + `poetry install` -> `just run` (uvicorn). alembic/versions/ contains real migrations and the justfile defines a `migrate` recipe (`just migrate` -> `alembic upgrade head`), but the README never references it.

suspectedDrift.what: Setup depends on the `just` command runner, not preinstalled on a base Linux image
suspectedDrift.evidence: README.md 'Setup just' assumes `apt install just` (Debian/Ubuntu); the `just` apt package isn't present on every minimal Debian/Ubuntu base image/release by default, so this step can silently fail depending on the container's base image.

repos.why: Clean, modern, well-maintained template whose only real gaps are a skipped migration step and a non-default tool dependency — a useful mid-severity contrast to the higher-drift repos.

suspectedDrift.what: Stated Node floor is far older than what's actually CI-tested
suspectedDrift.evidence: package.json: `"engines": { "node": ">=10.x" }`; .github/workflows/test.yml matrix is `node-version: [18.x, 20.x]` — the version the package.json advertises as a floor has never been exercised in CI, and a container defaulting to a modern Node (22+) is equally untested against `mongoose ~5.13.20`.

repos.why: 1.8-year-stale, popular repo with a concrete, file-quotable version-floor vs CI-matrix mismatch — the canonical 'drifted engines field' case.

repos.readmeSetupSection: Getting started / Getting started, standard way (no containerization)

suspectedDrift.what: Stated Node version contradicts package.json's engines field
suspectedDrift.evidence: package.json: `"engines": { "node": ">=8.10.0" }`; README.md (standard-way section) says 'I develop the NET.ts project on node version 16' — two different floors, neither enforced, and no .nvmrc anywhere.

suspectedDrift.what: A real env file is committed instead of an example template
suspectedDrift.evidence: The repo tracks `.env.local` directly (not `.env.example`); the README's standard-way section tells you to 'set env variables defined in the .env.local file' and even suggests `export $(cat .env.local)`, treating a committed file as the secrets source.

repos.why: Small, stale (2.5y) boilerplate with two concrete, low-effort-to-spot version/secrets inconsistencies; fast install since the audited (master) branch needs no external services — MongoDB support only exists on a separate add_mongo branch.

suspectedDrift.what: OTP/email feature needs real SMTP creds that .env.example only stubs with placeholders
suspectedDrift.evidence: .env.example ships `EMAIL_SMTP_HOST=YourSMTPHost`, `EMAIL_SMTP_USERNAME=YourSMTPUsername`, etc. as literal placeholder strings (not blank); helpers/mailer.js and the register-with-OTP flow described in the README's Features list depend on them, but 'Setting up environments' never says these can be left as placeholders or are optional for basic server startup.

suspectedDrift.what: Stated Node/Mongo floor is unverifiable — no engines field, dead CI badge
suspectedDrift.evidence: README.md 'Software Requirements': 'Node.js 8+', 'MongoDB 3.6+ (Recommended 4+)'; package.json has no `engines` field at all; the README's Travis CI badge points at travis-ci.com, a service most open-source projects migrated off years ago, so there's no working CI confirming either claim.

repos.why: 3.4-year-stale, popular repo with an env-var-looks-mandatory-but-isn't gap that's a classic real-world false-blocker for a newcomer.

repos.readmeSetupSection: Prerequisites / Run project using Docker containers

suspectedDrift.what: A required settings field has no safe default; .env.example only ships an empty stub
suspectedDrift.evidence: backend/app/app/core/config.py:23 declares `OPENAI_API_KEY: str` (required, no default); backend/app/app/main.py:173 does `ChatOpenAI(temperature=0, openai_api_key=settings.OPENAI_API_KEY)`; .env.example:50 ships `OPENAI_API_KEY=` empty, and the README never flags the Langchain/chatbot feature (Table of Contents item 18) as optional or the key as skippable.

suspectedDrift.what: README states three slightly different Python version ranges in one document
suspectedDrift.evidence: README.md intro: 'fully compatible with Python >=3.10' and 'Python 3.10 and later versions'; the 'Prerequisites' section header itself is literally `## Python ">3.9,<3.12"`; backend/app/pyproject.toml:42 pins `python = ">3.9,<3.12"`.

repos.why: Heaviest stack in the set (Postgres+Redis+MinIO+Celery+Caddy) with a genuinely required-looking API key field — a good stress test of FirstRun's missing-secret handling, though setup takes longer than the others.

suspectedDrift.what: Pinned 2022-era dependency set with no transitive upper bounds
suspectedDrift.evidence: requirements.txt exact-pins `flask==2.2.2`, `flask-sqlalchemy==3.0.3`, `connexion[swagger-ui]==2.14.2`, `markupsafe==2.1.2` with nothing bounding transitive deps like Werkzeug/Jinja2 — a fresh pip install in 2026 can resolve incompatible newer versions of those.

suspectedDrift.what: A required manual DB-seed step lives only in the FAQ, not the Run section
suspectedDrift.evidence: README.md's own FAQ ('There is a database error upon reaching endpoints!') says you must first `GET /createdb`; this step is absent from the 'Run it' section itself, so following just that section literally leaves every endpoint erroring until you happen to read the FAQ.

repos.why: Small, actively maintained, mostly-works repo — a useful low-drift control point in the set, with only a soft dependency-pinning risk and an easy-to-miss FAQ-only step.

suspectedDrift.what: CI badge links through to a differently-named repo
suspectedDrift.evidence: README.md's CI badge target is `.../express-typescript/actions/workflows/ci.yml?branch=master`, but the badge's href resolves through `express-typescript-2024` (an older name/fork of this same project) — cosmetic, but a real inconsistency in the doc.

repos.why: Actively maintained (pushed days ago); `.tool-versions` and `.env.template` are both accurate and correctly referenced — best available 'should mostly just work' control example on the Node/TS side.

suspectedDrift.what: README's primary install path never exercises the checked-out commit
suspectedDrift.evidence: README.md 'Pip' section says `pip3 install jello`, which pulls the latest PyPI release rather than the code at this SHA; setup.py:18 pins `python_requires='>=3.6'`, generous enough that this is unlikely to be a real break, just a fidelity gap for the audit.

repos.why: Trivial, fast, near-guaranteed-pass control target; keeps the audit's total runtime down and contrasts with the higher-severity repos.

suspectedDrift.what: Shell-profile-editing steps assume an interactive login shell a container run doesn't provide
suspectedDrift.evidence: README.md Method 1 steps 3-4: `echo 'please' >> ~/.bashrc` then 'restart the terminal' to verify success; a non-interactive container test never sources ~/.bashrc that way, so the documented success check (a new terminal showing the please banner) can't fire even though the underlying `pip install please-cli` succeeded.

suspectedDrift.what: No pyproject-based local dev path documented despite one existing in the repo
suspectedDrift.evidence: pyproject.toml + poetry.lock exist for local development, but README.md 'Installation' only documents installing the published `please-cli` PyPI package or a downloaded release .whl — never `poetry install` against this checkout.

repos.why: 2.9-year-stale, trivial CLI, but the bashrc/interactive-shell assumption is a realistic 'works for a human, ambiguous for a container' case worth including.

suspectedDrift.what: Stated install path differs from how the repo is actually built/tested
suspectedDrift.evidence: README.md 'Installation' says `npm install -g git2txt` (a registry install of the published package); package.json's own `engines.node: >=18` and its `test` script (`chmod +x index.js && ava`) are never surfaced in the README, so a contributor following only the README wouldn't discover the Node 18 floor or how to run tests against this checkout.

repos.why: Tiny, fast clone; a clean low-risk control alongside jello and add-gitignore.

suspectedDrift.what: Depends on the long-deprecated `request` package with no Node version floor documented anywhere
suspectedDrift.evidence: package.json dependencies include `request: ^2.85.0` (deprecated by its maintainers Feb 2020, no updates since) and `inquirer: ^5.2.0` (five major versions behind current); there is no `engines` field in package.json, and README.md's only guidance is 'make sure you have NodeJS installed', with no version floor for either a very old or very new Node.

repos.why: 2.9-year-stale, trivial `npx` one-liner setup — fast and cheap, with plausible-but-low-severity drift that rounds out the mix.
